First public release.

fufu (`ff`) is a version control interface built on the belief that jj got the workflow right and git got the repository right — and that you can have both. git remains the VCS; fufu is the pilot. At every instant, the repository is a boring git repository — fufu never creates a state plain git cannot represent.

What's here:

- **Capture** — bare `ff` snapshots the working tree (untracked files included) as ordinary git objects; every other command captures first, then does its work. `ff log`, `ff restore`, `ff trim` walk, recover, and prune the timeline. `ff git <anything>` passes through with a capture at the boundary; `ff hook shell|agent install` wires the automatic triggers (shell alias, Claude Code hooks).
- **Time** — an operation journal and whole-repo undo: `ff undo` reverses the last operation, whatever it was. `ff commit`, `ff switch`, `ff new`, `ff branch`, `ff describe` move between lines of work without stashes or ceremony; tree memory keeps each branch's uncommitted work with the branch.

Install: see the [README](https://github.com/tyler-johnson/fufu#install) — `curl | sh`, PowerShell, or `brew install tyler-johnson/tap/fufu`.

Binaries for linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64, checksummed. Windows binaries are provided and CI-tested, but young. The design — what exists, what's coming, and why — lives in [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/tyler-johnson/fufu/blob/main/DESIGN.md).
